case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 14th February 1999 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 11827 of 1991.)
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the impugned order refusing to restore the civil revision No. 1827 of 1991 discharged for default.

2. Abdur Razaque Khan, learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the petitioners, submits that in view of the filing of two revisions against the impugned order of the Court of appeal below in respect of the selfsame suit for declaration of title in the suit land, the other civil revision No. 1826 of 1991 still remaining pending, the discharge of the instant Rule for failure to deposit the requisites would adversely affect the decision in the suit in case of the other Rule being made absolute resulting thereby a conflicting decision operating differently between the parties in respect of the suit land subject-matter of a single suit for declaration of title. The learned Additional Attorney-General has further submitted that the latches in taking steps was not due to the negligence of the law officer concern but was due to the delay in obtaining sanction for deposit of the requisite and, as such, the Rule is required to be restored for ends of justice.

<u>3. It appears that two Rules were issued against the judgment and decree of the appellate Court dated 28-7-1990 arising out of decree dated 31-8-1985 in a suit for declaration of title against the petitioners and both the Rules were ordered to be heard together and accordingly rules were issued upon plaintiffs. The matter came up before the Lawzima Court on 6-1-1992 but no one appeared on that date whereupon the Registrar passed an order for issuance of fresh notice by registered post directing to put in requisites with correct postal address within 20-1-1991 and failure to deposit the same by the date fixed the matter came up before the Court on 20-1-1992. As none appeared the Court accordingly passed the order allowing three weeks’ time to put in the requisite failing which the Rule shall stand discharged. Accordingly the Rule stood discharged after expiry of three weeks with effect from 20-7-1992 as no steps were taken. Thereafter, the petitioner did not take any steps within reasonable time but after a lapse of about 7 years on the plea that the matter was misplaced, an application for restoration vacating the order dated 20-7-1992 was filed. The High Court Division did not find the explanation satisfactory. The suit of the plaintiffs was decreed on 31-8-1985 and the appeal there from was dismissed on 27-8-1990. The Rule was discharged in 1992 but there was not explanation for unusual delay thereby accruing a vested right in the respondent. The High Court Division did not find favour with the explanation of long unusual delay in order to deprive a vested right to the plaintiff. The High Court Division in exercise of its discretion rejected the prayer for restoration of the Rule discharged for default.</u>

4. We did not find any cogent reason as well to disturb the impugned decision.

The petition is dismissed.

End.

Md Humayun Kabir Bulbul, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners.

full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-4, 7-13 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24-1-2004 (decree signed on 31-1-2004) passed by the Additional District Judge, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No. 68 of 1991 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 12-3-1991 (decree signed on 18-3-1991) passed by the Assistant Judge, Kachua, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 14 of 1998 dismissing the suit should not be set aside.

2. Material facts of the case, briefly, are that the petitioners as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 14 of 1998 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kachua, Bagerhat praying for declaration of their title in the suit land and perpetual injunction upon the defendants not to dispossess the plaintiffs thereto on the averments that the suit land under Kachua Police Station of Bhasha Mouza of CS Khatian No. 32 and SA Khatian No. 244, Dag No. 56 land measuring 0.47 acres was originally belonged to Asiruddin Mallik, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, that after the death of Asiruddin Mallik his wife Saju Begum, son Jabbar Mallik and 4 daughters namely Faku Bibi, Maju Bibi, Saju Bibi and Moina Bibi inherited the said land and subsequently, on demise of Jabbar Mallik and Saju Begum (wife of late Asiruddin), the said 4 daughters of Late Asiruddin Mallik remained as successor, that the plaintiffs (two full brother) having purchased the suit land from the daughters of Asiruddin Mallik vide two registered kabala deeds dated 13-1-87 and 1-4-87 and became for owner and possessor the same, that the defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit land but the SA record was published mistakenly in the name of some defendants and thereupon, the defendants claimed the suit land and also threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs; that the plaintiffs were not aware about the wrong SA record and due to this the plaintiffs did not face any difficulty but very recently the defendants have claimed the suit land disclosing that the SA record was published in their name and hence that suit.

3. The defendant Nos. 1-4 and 7-13 entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement denying all the materials allegations of the plaint contending interalia, that Asiruddin Mallik, the predecessors of the plaintiffs on 20th Jaistha, 1339 BS by an unregistered deed sold the suit land to one Babor Ali, the predecessors of the defendants and after the death of the said Babor Ali, the defendants as his legal heirs inherited the suit land and thereupon, the SA record has been published correctly in their name including the names of their predecessor and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. Upon the pleadings of the parties, the learned Assistant Judge, Kachua, Bagerhat framed 6 (six) issues namely:—

(1) Whether the suit is maintainable in its present form?

(2) Whether the suit is barred by limitation?

(3) Whether the suit is bad for defect of parties?

(4) Whether the suit is valued properly and Court fees are correct?

(5) Whether the plaintiffs have right, title and possession in the suit land?

(6) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get the relief as prayed for?

5. At the trial both the parties led evidences both oral and documentary to prove their respective cases. The learned Assistant Judge on consideration of the materials on record dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 12-3-1991 on the ground that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit land.

6. On appeal, the learned Additional District Judge, Bagerhat by his judgment and decree dated 24-1-2004 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge, Kachua, Bagerhat. Against which the plaintiff-petitioners have come before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr Md Humayun Kabir Bulbul, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that both the Courts below committed an error of law in passing the impugned judgments in failing to appreciate the case of the respective parties in its true perspective, resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice as such, the same are liable to be set aside. He next in the course of argument after placing the materials on record submits that the judgments of two Courts below are based on total non-consideration of the materials evidence on record and the findings of the Courts below are shockingly perverse to the extent that the plain-tiffs could not prove their possession in the suit landinspite of sufficient corroborative evidence to indicate that the plaintiffs are in possession over the suit property. Drawing my attention to the judgment of the trial Court below Mr Humayun Kabir submits that from a reading of the judgment of the trial Court there is no reason to believe that the plaintiffs cloud not prove their case but in the end the trial Court abruptly arrived at a finding that' the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit land which is perverse being contrary to law, evidence and materials on record.

8. Mr Humayun Kabir, further submits that PW 2 proved 2 registered kabala deeds, rent receipts but the Courts below committed wrong in discarding the same without assigning any reason whatsoever which occasioned a failure of justice. The learned Advocate then referring to the evidence of PWs submits that both the Courts below did not at all consider the evidence of PWs namely, PW 1, PW 2, PW 3 and PW 4 in its true perspective since all them testified in one voice that the plaintiffs are in possession over the suit land and PW 2, proved the registered kabala deeds dated 13-1-87 and 1-4-87 as Exhibit Nos. 3 and 3(Ka). Drawing my attention to the evidence of DWs namely DW and DW 2 Mr Humayun Kabir points out that the DWs are not only made inconsistent statement with regard to their so-called unregistered kabala deed they also could not produce any document in support of their so-called unregistered deed before the trial Court but in spite of that the Courts below most illegally relying on the evidence of DWs dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession over the suit land. Mr Humayun Kabir, relying on the decision reported in 19 DLR 9 and 59 DLR 207 submits that the defendants claimed their right, title over the suit and on the basis of SA record which appears to be prepared wrongly in their name at the early period of the than Pakistan but such record of rights does neither create nor destroy the right, title and possession as acquired by the plaintiff-petitioners on the basis of two registered kabala deeds dated 13-1-87 and 1-4-87 as Exhibit Nos. 3 and 3(Ka). He further adds that the SA record is not a conclusive evidence which is mere a record of physical possession at the time when it is prepared.

9. Mr Humayun Kabir, also points out that both the Courts below gave importance to the in-consistence oral evidence of DWs over the documentary evidences, thus committed an error, resulting in the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate finally contends that since there being a total non-consideration of the material evidence on record both oral and documentary it is incumbent of this Court sitting under provisional jurisdiction to consider the same in order to arrive at a proper finding on the basis of the materials on record.

10. On the other hand, Mrs Nurun Nahar, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-respondent-opposite parties by filing counter affidavit supports the impugned judgments of two Courts below which were, according to him just, correct and proper. The learned Advocate, thereafter, submits that both the Courts below concurrently arrived at a finding that the plaintiffs miserably failed to prove their possession over the suit land by adducing evidence which are, in-fact, based on correct evaluation of facts and the materials of the case.

11. Mrs Nurun Nahar, further submits that at the trial the defendant-opposite parties in order to prove their right, title and possession exhibited 9(nine) Dakhilas and admittedly, the SR record was prepared in their name as well as in the name of their predecessor and, as such, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgments of 2 (two) Courts below. The learned Advocate finally submits that in this case the plaintiff-petitioners could not produce the bia-deeds and that on this score also the plaintiff-petitioner miserably failed to prove their right, title in the suit land. Mrs Nahar, the learned Advocate to strengthen her submission has relied on the decisions reported in 10 MLR (AD) 100, 6 MLR 6, 35 DLR (AD) 216 and 37 DLR (AD) 202.

12. I have gone through the contentions of the provisional application, counter-affidavit and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the respective parties. Now, the real question for consideration in this case, whether the judgments of two Courts below are based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case. I have already noticed that the trial Court dismissed the suit on the sole ground that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit land.

13. It is found that in this case plaintiffs examined in all 4(four) witnesses namely PW 1, PW 2, PW 3 and PW 4 and the defendants examined 2(two). witnesses namely DW 1 and DW 2. On perusal of the materials on record, it appears that the trial Court found after discussion of the evidence on record that the plaintiffs had adduced evidence only one witness namely PW 4 to prove their possession in the suit land, who in a half-hearted manner narrated about the possession of the plaintiffs. The Court of appeal below in its turn also affirmed the decision of the trial Court.

14. Now, let me discuss the evidence of PWs in order to resolve the issue whether the impugned judgments of two Courts below are based on correct and proper appreciation of the evidence and materials on record on the point of possession. On going through the materials on record, it appears that plaintiff No. 1, Esahaq Ali Mallik himself was examined as PW 1, who stated that after the death of Asiruddin Mallik his heirs namely Maju Bibi (wife), 4 (four) daughters namely Faku, Maju, Saju and Moyna and one son Jabbar inherited the suit land and Faku, Maju and Saju Bibi transferred 0.36 acres of land to the plaintiffs by a registered deed and Moyna Bibi also transferred her portion of land by executing another registered kabala deed. This witness also stated that after execution of the deeds they handed over the possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs. This witness also stated that :

"আমরা সম্পূর্ণ জমি ভোগ দখল করি । " PW 2, Mosharraf Mallik, who stated that : " সাজু, মাজু আমার প্রতিবেশী এবং একই বয়সের মেয়ে । সাজু, মাজু, ফকু বিবি ৩ জনে জমি ১/২ নং বাদীদের বরাবর কবলা দেয় । তাও জানি । আমি পরিচিত ছিলাম । ৪ বৎসর আগে পৌষ মাসের শেষে দিকে দখল দেয় । সাজু, মাজু এবং ফকু বিবি আমার সামনে টিপ দেয় ।  "

PW-3, Sabed Ali Sheikh, stated that Moyna Bibi is her cousin's wife, who transferred the suit land to the plaintiffs. He identified the signature of Moyna Bibi and proved her signature as Exhibit 'Ka'. This witness in his cross-examination denied the suggestion that the possession of the suit land was not handed over infamous of the plaintiffs. PW 4, Sohrab Hossain, stated in his deposition that :

বাদী এবং বিবাদীদের এবং নালিশি জমি চিনি । না: জমি ইসহাক মল্লিক দখল করে । এর আগে ১ নং বাদীর বাবাকে দখল করতে দেখেছি । বিবাদীদের নালিশি জমি দখল করতে দেখিনি ।

15. It is also found that the plaintiffs in order to prove their right, title in the suit land exhibited two registered deeds namely Exhibit 3 and 3(Ka) and CS Khatian recorded in the name of late Asiruddin Mallik, the predecessor of the plaintiff-petitioners and also exhibited rent receipt vide Exhibit 1.

<u>16. The above quoted evidence of PWs. Shows that all the PWs it their respective evidence disclosed that the plaintiff-petitioners are in possession of the suit land. Therefore, in any view of the matter it can be safely said that the finding of the learned Assistant Judge that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession by adducing evidence over the suit land is, in-fact, not based on proper appreciation of the evidence and materials of the case. Therefore, I find substance in the submission of Mr Humayun Kabir Bulbul that the Trial Court below fell into an error of law and facts dismissing the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit land.</u>

17. It is found from the evidence of the defendant witnesses that DW 1, Tobarek Sheikh, in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 2(two) blank papers but DW 2, Mr Aladdin Sheikh in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 1 (one) blank paper. On the face of these inconsistencies, it is difficult to rely upon their testimony. It is also found that the trial Court as well as appellate Court below as last Court of fact having not been addressed this aspect of the case.

18. It is also found that defendants did not or could not produce their unregistered deed on the plea that during liberation war their unregistered deed was looted away. It appears that DW 1, in his cross-examination stated that with regard to missing their deed relating to the suit land he did not make any general diary. The Court of appeal below on this point observed as follows :

অত্র মামলায় দাখিলী না : জমির খাজনার দাখিলা যাহা বিবাদী গণের নিকট ছিল সেইগুলি ১৯৭১ সালে তর্কিত দলিলের সহিত হারায় নাই বলিয়া তর্কিত কবলে দলিলের অস্তিত্ব সম্পর্কে সন্দেহের সৃষ্টি হয় । তর্কিত কবলে দলিল মুলে না : জমি বাবদ মালেক জমিদার সেরেস্তায় কোন খাজনার দাখিলা দাখিল করা হয় নাই । এইরূপ অবস্থায় বিবাদীর পূর্ববর্তী বাবর আলী ১৩৩৯ সালের ২০ শে জ্যৈষ্ঠ অরেজি : কৃত কবলা মুলে না: জমিতে স্বত্ববান হওয়ার বিষয়ে সন্দেহ থাকিলেও উক্ত অরেজি: কৃত দলিলের ভিত্তিতে না : জমিতে বিবাদীর পূর্ববর্তী নামে না: জমি বাবদ এস, এ, রেকর্ডের ভিত্তিতে বিবাদীপক্ষ খাজনাদি প্রদ : ক(৮) আদায় করিয়া যথারীতি না : আছে তাহা প্রতীয়মান হয় ।

19. From the above quoted observations of the appellate Court together with the above quoted evidence of DWs. I find no possible reason to hold that the defendant-opposite parties have succeeded to prove their right, title or possession in the suit land. Therefore, I am inclined to hold that the both the Courts below erred in law in dismissing the suit without properly applying their judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decisions occasioning failure of justice.

20. There is another aspect of the case which needs to be addressed as it involves and important question of law. It is contended that the SA record has been published correctly in name of some defendants including their predecessor.

21. In the case of Abdul Jabbar vs Abdul Aziz reported in 19 DLR 9, it has been held that : "It is not certainly conclusive evidence of the state of things appearing in the record of right, or in other words, it is not conclusive evidence of correctness of the entries in the record of rights."

22. In the case of Dhaka City Corporation vs Shamsur Rahman reported in 59 DLR 207, wherein it has been held that : "Such view of the trial Court was reversed rightly by the appellate Court. Because, the decision of the trial Court is based on no authority. Earlier, wrong record of rights could be corrected by a mere application under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. In such proceeding, the aggrieved party was never required to establish title to get an order for correction of the record of rights. Reason is not far away to find. Record of rights does neither create nor destroy title. It is mere a record of physical possession at the time when it is prepared."

23. From a reading of the above quoted decision, it transpires that the SA record is not a conclusive evidence to prove the right, title and possession in the suit land. It is mere a record of physical possession at the time where it is prepared.

24. In the facts and circumstances of the case as I have discussed above vis-a-vis the above quoted decisions, I am of the opinion that the appellate Court below committed wrong in holding that:

“এইরূপ অবস্থায় বিবাদীর পূর্ববর্তী বাবর আলী ১৩৩৯ সালের ২০ শে জ্যৈষ্ঠ অরেজি : কৃত কবলে মুলে না: জমিতে সত্যবান হওয়ার বিষয়ে সন্দেহ থাকিলেও উক্ত অরেজি : কৃত দলিলের ভিত্তিতে না : জমিতে বিবাদীর পূর্ববর্তী নামে না: জমি বাবদ এস, এ, রেকর্ডের ভিত্তিতে বিবাদীপক্ষ খাজনাদি প্রদ : ক(৮) আদায় করিয়া যথারীতি না : আছে তাহা প্রতীয়মান হয় ।”

This finding is plainly misconceived. The registered kabala deeds of the plaintiffs should not be thrown in liming mere on the basis of oral evidence.

25. Law is now well settled that the burden lies on the plaintiff to prove his case and he must succeed on his own strength and not at the weakness of the defendant.

<u>26. I have already indicated that in this case the plaintiff-petitioners by adducing sufficient evidence both oral and documentary proved their right, title and possession in the suit land. The secondary evidence of a document is admissible in the cases specially mentioned in section 65 of the Evidence Act and if the original is not available, reasons for non-availability must be given but in this case, I have already noticed that the defendants neither produced their unregistered deed nor produced any documentary evidence to show that their original un-registered deed in lost More so, as I have already observed the DW 1, Tobarek Sheikh, in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 2(two) blank papers and DW 2, Md Aladdin Sheikh stated in his deposition stated that their un-registered deed was written on 1(one) blank paper. These contradictions and inconstancies on material point in the facts of the present case create serious doubt upon the genuineness of the alleged unregistered deed of the defendant-opposite parties. It is also found that the Courts below did not address to this most important aspect of the case at all.</u>

27. Now, it remains for me to consider decisions cited by Mrs Nurun Nahar, the learned Advocate for the defendant-opposite parties. I have carefully gone through the cited decisions namely the decisions reported in 10 MLR (AD) 100, 6 MLR 6, 35 DLR (AD) 216 and 37 DLR (AD) 202 to the best of my ability and I find that the principles as enunciated in those decisions have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the instant case inasmuch as facts of those case are quite distinguishable from the facts of the present case.

<u>28. For all the above reasons the impugned judgments and decree of the 2 (two) Courts below cannot be sustained.</u>

29. Accordingly, the Rule succeeds.

30. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 24-1-2004 (decree signed on 31-1-2004) passed by the Additional District Judge, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No. 68 of 1991 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 12-3-1991 (decree signed on 18-3-1991) passed by the Assistant Judge, Kachua, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 14 of 1998 dismissing the suit are set aside.

Let a copy of the judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J : This rule by plaintiff of Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 filed for specific performance of contract, against principal defendants-appellant of Appeal from Original Decree No. 6 of 2009, directed against judgment and order dated 25-4-2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur allowing Miscellaneous Case No. 455 of 2008 filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure thereby set-aside the judgment and decree dated 29-4-2008 subject matter of Appeal from Original Decree No. 6 of 2009.

2. The aforesaid suit was suit was filed by the plaintiff petitioner against defendant No. 1, Mst. Rana Noor, for specific performance of contract in which Government of Bangladesh was made proforma-defendant. The suit was decreed. Rana Noor defendant No. 1, having aggrieved filed the Appeal from Original Decree No. 6 of 2009 which is pending before this Court. While decree was passed on 29-4-2008, as Government of Bangladesh was made proforma defendant, did not appear filed Miscellaneous Case No. 455 of 2008 on 20-10-2008 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Appeal was tendered on 7-1-2009. Defendant No. 1 also obtained an order of stay of the execution proceedings on 20-10-2009.

3. In the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is stated that Government having been made proforma defendant did not take proper attention to the summons which was served on the Government, as such, government did not take proper care and step in the proceeding of the suit. It is specific case of the Government that,

“যেহেতু নালিশী সম্পত্তি পুরোটাই সরকারী সম্পত্তি। তৎকালীন প্রধান মন্ত্রী শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান ঢাকা-টাঙ্গাইল সড়কের পাশে মৌচাকে অবস্তিত নুরবার্গ কৃষি খামারটি একটি পরিত্যাক্ত সম্পত্তি হিসেবে ঘোষনা করেন এবং কৃষি মন্ত্রনালয় খামারের উন্নয়ন ও সংরক্ষনের দায়িত্বগ্রহন করবেন এবং গনপূর্ত মন্ত্রণালয় তন্মধ্যে অবস্থিত হেড অফিসের রেষ্ট হাউজের যথোপযুক্ত সংস্কার এবং সংরক্ষন করিবেন বলে ৩-৭-১৯৭২ইং তারিখে লিখিত নির্দেশ প্রদান করেন।

যেহেতু পরবর্তীতে ১৯৭৩ সালে দি বাংলাদেশ গেজেট এর মাধ্যমে মার্চ ৮ তারিখ ১৯৭৩ সনে বাংলাদেশ বনশিল্প উন্নয়ন করপারেশন নামে গেজেট ভুক্ত হয় এবং এপি ১/৮০ কেস মূলে বনশিল্প উন্নয়ন কর্পোরেশন এর বরাবরে লীজ প্রদান করা হয়। বনশিল্প ও শিল্প উন্নয়ন কর্পোরেশন বছর বছর ৪.৪৬ একর জমির লীজ মানি পরিশোধ করে আসিতেছে এবং বলে রহিয়াছে। সব কিছু জানা সত্ত্বেও সহকারী সম্পত্তি আত্মসাত করার জন্য সকল তথ্য গোপন করে ভূয়া, বায়নাপত্র সৃজন পূর্বক মিথ্যা চুক্তি প্রবলের মোকদ্দমাটি অত্র দরখাস্তকারীর বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা রায় ও ডিক্রী হাসিল করেন। বিধায় রায় ও ডিক্রী রদ রহিত যোগ্য। সরকার পক্ষ জনাব দিয়া মুল মামলা প্রতিদ্বন্দিতা করিলে দেঃ মোঃ ১১/০৫ এ কোন প্রতিকার পাওয়ার সুযোগ নাই। প্রতিপক্ষ দুরভিসন্ধিমূলক ভাবে সরকারকে মোকাবিলা বিবাদী না করিয়া চুক্তি প্রবেলের মোকদ্দমা দায়ের না করিলে অত্র দরখাস্তকারীপক্ষ অবশ্যই দেওয়ানী ১১/০৫নং মোকদ্দমায় প্রতিদ্বন্ধিতা করিত। কিন্তু ধুবন্ধব বাদী প্রতিপক্ষ সরকারী সম্পত্তি আত্মসাৎ করার জন্য ভূয়া বায়নাপত্র সৃজন করিয়া সরকার পক্ষকে মোকাবিলা বিবাদী করিয়া প্রতারনামূলক ভাবে একতরফা ডিক্রী হাসিল করায় দরখাস্তকারী পক্ষের অপুরনীয় ক্ষতির কারন হইয়াছে।”

4. In this Miscellaneous Case, plaintiff appeared and filed written objection. There-after, disappeared. Learned Joint District Judge while allowing the Miscellaneous Case found inter alia that, since defendant Government was not made principal defendant but proforma defendant, Government did not take proper step in the proceeding of the suit. The finding of the learned Joint District Judge is that :—

"Defendants could not take proper steps in the suit. The suit properties are government properties. The Plaintiff-opposite-parties proclaimed in the area that he had got decree in the suit regarding the Government properties. The defendants inquired about the matter and according to the information slip they got information that the suit was decreed on contest on 29-4-2008. The PW 1 gives deposition supporting the above claim of the partition. The information slips (Exhibit-2) so that the defendants-opposite parties came to know about impugned decree on 16-10-2008. This case was filed on 20-10-2008. Since this case was filed within 30 (thirty) days from the date of knowledge of impugned decree, the case is not barred by limitation. The record and documents also so that the defendants petitioners were proforma defendants in the case and the suit properties appear to be government properties. Since the petitioners were not made principal defendants, there was made a situation that they did not contest the suit earlier. So it can be said that there were sufficient reasons behind their non-appearance in the suit. Accordingly points No. 2 and 3 are decided in favour of the petitioners.

<u>5. Rule 13 Order IX speaks 'satisfaction' and this 'satisfaction' is satisfaction of the Court. From the facts of the case it appears that Government satisfactorily explained its non-appearance when the suit was decreed against Government.</u>

6. President's Order No. 142 of 1972 after amendment incorporated section 6 which is as :—

"No person shall, without joining the Government which shall be a necessary party, file or proceed with any suit.

(a) for the specific performance of any contract relating to the transfer of any immoveable property or for declaration of title to, or assertion of ownership of, any such property."

<u>7. On a reading of this law it appears that the aforesaid law before amendment government was impleaded as proforma defendant but after amendment, government became necessary party, as such, we find that learned Judge committed no illegality in allowing the Miscellaneous Case and set-aside the ex-parte decree for fresh trial of Title Suit No. 11 of 2005. We find no substance in the rule.</u>

8. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

9. Appeal from Original Decree No. 6 of 2009 arisen having been arisen from the same judgment, become infructuous. We have already noticed the judgment and decree dated 294-2008 passed in Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 out of which the appeal arisen, having set-aside the appeal is dismissed as it become infructuous.

10. Learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur directed to dispose of Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 within 1 (one) year from the date of receive of this judgment.

11. Send down the lower court records.

Communicate this order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This appeal at the instant of defendant-appellant directed against judgment and decree dated 22-11-2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Paribesh Court, Chittagong decreeing Other Suit No. 146 of 2004.

2. Short facts relating for disposal of this appeal are that, the original owner of schedule to the plaint land were Mohontara Debi, Promoda Bala Debi and Sudhir Ranjan Nath who sold the suit land to Lal Miah, Chand Miah and Younus Miah by registered deed No. 567 dated 28-1-1951. Lal Miah and his other three brothers purchased 80 decimals of land of RS khatian No. 153 by kabala deed No. 566 on 21-1-1951. Lal Miah died leaving three brothers, Younus Miah, Chand Miah and Kala Miah and 2 sisters, Safia Khatun and Samana Khatun to inherit his share in the suit property. Wife, sons and daughters of Lal Miah died in a road accident in 1966. After the death of Lal Miah, Younus Miah and Chand Miah amicably partitioned the suit land of RS khatian No. 519 and while they were in possession their respective shares were sold, 0.0750 decimals of land by kabala deed Nos. 5286 and 5359 dated 14-3-1983 and 15-3-1983 to Abul Kalam Chowdhury and possession was delivered. Later on, Younus Miah by kabala deed No. 2545 dated 28-8-1983 sold 0.05 decimals of land from RS dag No. 519 to Habibur Rahman. Abul Kalam Chowdhury and Habibur Rahman mutated their names and open PS khatian No. 209 in their names. Abul Kalam Chowdhury by kabala deed No. 6080 dated 24-4-1989 sold 0.025 decimals of land from RS dag No. 519 and Habibur Rahman also sold similar quantum of land from same dag by kabala deed No. 603 dated 25-6-1989 to plaintiff No. 2 and delivered possession. Abul Kalam Chowdhury sold 0.0250 decimals of land to plaintiff No. 1, sold similar quantum of land by kabala deed No. 1800 dated 06-5-1989 to plaintiff No. 3, similar quantum of land from same dag by kabala No. 602 dated 06-8-1989 and delivered possession. Habibur Rahman also sold similar quantum of land from same dag to plaintiff No. 3 by kabala deed No. 603 dated 24-6-1989. In this way plaintiffs by 5 registered deeds purchased 1250 decimals of land from R.S. dag No. 519 and became owner and possessor and constructed pucca boundary wall, possessing the suit land having their title there to, they mutated their names and opened PS khatian No. 209/10 and paying rents regularly. In the aforesaid 5 purchase deeds, PS Khatian having been rightly recorded, they sold the purchased land to Abul Kalam Chowdhury and Habibur Rahman on 27-12-1989 and by correction deed No. 1765 corrected the same. Defend-ant No. 2 on 04-4-1995 published auction notice through "Daily Azadi" in respect of schedule No B to the suit land which was published pursuant to Mortgage Execution Case No. 27 of 1998. On query plaintiffs could know that defendant falsely showing Khorgled Miah, son of Lal Miah, Kashem Miah, son of Chand Miah and Mohammad Hossain, son of Younus Miah as owners, mortgaged the land of plaintiff to defendant No. 1 Bank. Bank by instituting Artha Rin Case No. 35 of 1995 got ex-parte decree and published notice. Lal Miah had no son named Khorshed Miah and Younus Miah had no son named Mohammad Hossain and there was no person in the name of defendant Nos. 4, 5 and 6 in the suit land and the aforesaid fictitious person earlier also committed similar type of activities. Plaintiffs prayed for decree as:-

"(a) that a declaratory decree be passed in favour of the plaintiffs and against the defendants declaring plaintiffs title in respect of the schedule 'B' land.

(b) That it be further declared that the preliminary decree and final decree dated 22-3-98 and 27-5-98 respectively of Mortgage Suit No. 35 of 1995 is void, in operative and in effective so far it relates to schedule 'B' land of the plaintiffs and plaintiffs and their 'B' schedule land are not bound by the aforesaid preliminary decree and final decree dated 22-3-98 and 27-5-98 of Mortgage. Suit No. 35 of 1995 of 1st Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong."

3. In the suit although defendant-appellant filed written statement but defendant-appellant did not examined any witness.

4. Since defendant did not examined any witness in support of its written statement we left aside from consideration the written statement filed by defendant.

5. Plaintiff examined 4 witnesses and exhibited a number of deeds. Defendant did not file any document along with the written statement. Learned Judge decreed the suit holding that in obtaining ex-parte decree fraud has been perpetuated in giving mortgage the suit land and since fraud has been detected it vitiate everything.

6. Mr. Khalilur Rahman Bhuiyan, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant-appellant, canvass before us, the law point that as per section 20 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the suit as filed is not maintainable. Learned Advocate further submits that it is admitted position that plaintiffs are 3rd party and as per section 32 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 plaintiffs could file application by paying 10% decreetal amount and challenged the mortgage deed and veracity of the of decree obtained ex-parte. Mr. Khalilur Rahman Bhuiyan, learned Advocate in support of his submissions relied on the decision of Jalaluddin Ahmed vs Md Selim Hossain, 7 ADC 291 and also the case of Harunur Rashid Bhuiyan vs Pubali Bank Ltd, 15 BLC 458. It is held that

"Since the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 being a special statute and there is specific provision for submitting any claim of a third party in any execution case arisen out of a decree or, an order of the Artha Rin Adalat the Courts below having rightly directed the petitioner to deposit 25% of the decretal amount as security otherwise, the application shall stand rejected and we endorse the reasoning."

7. Mr. Khijir Ahmed, learned. Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, submits, that, Artha  Rin Adalat Ain 2003 altogether do not debar the right of 3rd party of suit to challenge the veracity, legality and propriety of a decree passed by Artha Rim Adalat on the ground of fraud. Learned Advocate further submits that on question of law which has not been, within the frame work of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, in that premises suit can be maintainable. Learned Advocate refer to the decision of Chaina Arjuman Banu vs Rupali Bank Limited, reported in 14 BLD 321 and unreported decision of this Court passed in the case of Janata Bank Limited vs Faizul Mowla, First Misc. Appeal No. 291 of 2005 passed on 25-7-2010.

8. The submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties led us to consider the legal point i.e. some provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. It is to be borne in mind that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is special law. It is also known that Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 that suit instituted for realization of money disburse by financial institution. Section 3 of the Ain speaks that this law is supreme law on this subject. Section 5 of the Ain gives sole jurisdiction of Artha Rin Adalat for realization of loan of the financial institutions i.e. it can be said that it give exclusive jurisdiction of the Court i.e. Artha Rin Adalat in the matter of, realisation of loan by financial institute and if any decree passed that have supremacy over other law which has been clearly and in unambiguity declared in section 20 of the AM which runs as:-

"no question shall raised against in jurisdiction proceeding or any order, judgment, or decree shown in that Aurtha Rin Adalat Ain in any civil court or by any authority except under provision of this Act; if any prayer is submitted or any application is given for redressing grievances in any court or any authority ignoring the provision of this Act shall not be entertained or admitted by any court or authority On a reading of this section it can be said that if any illegal decree be passed from Artha Rin Adalat it can be challenge by the aggrieved party to a court constituted under this Act. But, when a private individual be affected who is not a party to the suit where his remedy lies as this Act only allowed financial institute to file suit/ case. So, a 3rd party cannot invoke section 20 of the Act to redress his grievances. Law makers make provision for 3rd party aggrieved by a decree under section 32. Section 32, objection against execution runs as:—

(i) If any third party, files claim according to the provision of Code of Civil Procedure in any execution case arisen out of a decree or an order of the Artha Rin Adalat and if the court does not outright rejects the same on its first consideration, the decree holder may submit prayer within a maximum period of 30 days for a hearing against the same by filling written objection.

(ii) In case of submission as above, the applicant shall deposit 10% money of the decretal amount or submit a bond for the same, failing which the demand shall not be entertained.

(iii) If the Artha Rin Adalat accepts any claim for consideration, the Court shall dispose of the said 'written objection' within 30 days of filing the same and if it fails to dispose of the matter within 30 days, the time shall be extended for more 30 days recording sufficient cause thereof.

(iv) The court while disposing the written objection under sub-section (iii) if observes that the claim under sub-section (i) has been met up with the dishonest intention to delay or to stop recovery of decretal money, then the court shall reject the petition and by the same order shall forfeit the deposited money or bond, submitted under Sub-section (ii) and the forfeited deposit or bond shall be recovered in such a manner as the decretal money is recovered and shall be paid to the decree-holder."

9. After conclusion of the submission of the objecting party in the suit, Adalat shall if objection sustained pass necessary order. So far we see that Artha Rin Adalat is supreme law on the subject, decision can be challenged under Code of Civil Procedure before the Adalat constituted under this Ain and provision of Civil Procedure can be apply subject to the provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Section 32 provide for certain legal formalities to perform before filing objection in executing the decree.

10. In the case of Harunur Rashaid Bhuiyan vs Pubali Bank Ltd, 15 BLC 458, it is held—

"In this connection, we asked the learned Advocate for the petitioner to enlighten us as to how the petitioner would not be treated as 3rd party in the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject keeping in mind that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 being a special statute providing special forum for realisation of loan granted by financial institution. Mr. Khair Ezaz Maswood has failed to lay his hands on any provision of the Ain, 2003 empowering the Adalat to accept his plea or grievance."

In the case of Jalaluddin Ahmed vs Md. Selim Hossain, 7 BLC 291, wherein it is argued—

"Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that since the petitioners who are real owners of the property not being made parties in the suit, they had no knowledge about the decree and the sale of the property in auction and therefore, they are entitled to make an application under Order XXI, Rule 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of possession but the High Court Division on a misconception of law interfered with the judgment of the learned District Judge on the reasoning that their application under Order XXI, Rule 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not sustainable in law. Mr. Bhuiyan further contended that since the petitioners are not claiming through the judgment debtors, they could have maintained an application under Order XXI, Rule 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of possession and thus, the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law holding that their application was not maintainable. Mr Bhuiyan finally argued that since the petitioners are the third party claimants, they are not required to deposit 25% of the decreetal amount in view of section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and the learned Judge of the High Court Division on a misconception of law held that the petitioners applicant is not maintainable without making deposit of 25% of the decreetal amount."

11. The Appellate Division held—

"Heard the learned Counsel and perused the materials on record. In view of section 32(1) Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the petitioners were required to deposit 25% of the decreetal amount while making an application for restoration of possession and in that view of the matter, the learned Judges of the High Court Division had committed no error in law in interfering with the judgment of the learned District Judge. Since the petitioners are not claiming title through the judgment debtors, this judgment will not stand on the way if they file a fresh suit, for recovery of the suit property. This leave petition is dismissed with the above observations."

12. In an earlier decision, Chaina Arjuman Banu vs Rupali Bank Limited, 14 BLD 321, relied by Mr Khijir Ahmed, it is held—

"We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the application as well as the connected papers. Since the bar as stated by the learned Subordinate Judge is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the case and since the suit is at the stage of final disposal, we are of the view that ends of justice will be met if we direct the learned Subordinate Judge to hear and dispose of the suit within reasonable time and in the meantime further proceedings of Money Execution case be stayed."

13, In the unreported decision of Appeal from Original Decree No. 291 of 2005, Janata Bank vs Faiaul Mowla, judgment delivered on 25-7-2012, a Division Bench of this Court, in which, one of us was a party, observed as:—

"On the other hand, Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Advocate on referring to the exhibits, submits that, suit was not filed against present plaintiffs nor against defendant Nos. 26 to 28 but against loanee, which is M/s. Chowdhury Enterprise and in the mortgage deed and in the other charge documents, Chowdhury enterprise executed everything for getting the loan, as such the properties of these plaintiffs cannot be put into auction to satisfy the execution proceeding.

It appears from the papers before us that defendant-appellant did not examine any witness nor file any papers is support of its claim. From exhibit 16 Ka it appears that mortgage suit was filed against M/s. Chowdhury Enterprise and present plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 4 to 6 were not included as principal defendant. From the plaint of that mortgage suit it appears that it was filed by Janata Bank against M/s. Chowdhury Enterprise."

<u>14. On a reading of the aforesaid judgments it appears there are two distinct opinions on question of law for filing of suit by aggrieved 3rd party against decree, either con-tested or ex parte and there is divergent of opinion regarding the jurisdiction of civil court in challenging the decree obtained in Aurtha Rin Adalat. It is the case of plaintiffs that decree was obtained by practicing fraud then why the plaintiffs shall pay, at present 10% of decreetal amount, for challenging the decree which obtained by practicing fraud under section 32 of the Ain. The civil court under section 9 of Civil Procedure Code has jurisdiction to try all suit/case of civil nature, as such, if the decree under challenge be tainted with fraud then why the plaintiff shall be over burden with compulsory payment of 10% of the decreetal amount as per section 32 of the Ain. It is now become a practice on the banking side that without satisfying or verifying the title of the mortgage deed, Bank disbursed loan to the applicant like nine pins and put the 3rd party like present one in extreme danger. On the facts of the given case we are of the view that since Artha Rin Adalat Ain, being special law, learned Subordinate Judge was totally on wrong forum in entertaining Other Suit No. 146 of 2004 which not within his jurisdiction. We are of the view that if Artha Rin Adalat passed a decree it can be challenged within the four corner of the Ain itself. The question raised is of great public importance as such although we allowed the appeal but giving certificate to the plaintiff to settle the dispute finally before the Appellate Division.</u>

15. With this observation the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost.

16. We will not sign the judgment within 2 (two) months from today and give further direction that decree passed by Artha Rin Adalat shall be stayed for this period.

17. Judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Paribesh Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No, 146 of 2004 is set-aside.

Send down the lower court records. Communicate this order at once.

End.

Vs.

full_judgment:
M Moazzam Husain J: This Rule was issued at the instance of the judgment-debtor petitioner calling in question an Order dated 13-11-2002 passed by the Joint District judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Panchagarh, in Money Execution Case No. 8 of 2002.

2. The backdrop of facts giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the decree-holder opposite party obtained on 13-9-1988 a money decree of Tk.2,36,761.50 against the present petitioner No.1 in Money Suit No.2 of 1988 passed by the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Panchagarh. The suit was for realization of Tk.1, 93,472.50 taken by the petitioner No.1 (judgment-debtor) from the opposite party Bank (decree-holder) against a small oil mill project. Pursuant to failure of the judgment-debtor to pay off the money the Bank initiated Money Execution Case No. 21 of 1993 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.1 Panchagarh. During pendency of the execution case the judgment-debtor along with his two full brothers (petitioner Nos. 2 and 3) filed on 29-1-1994 a joint petition (Annex-B) in the execution case stating, inter nlia, that following a negotiation between the judgment-debtor, his brothers and the highest authority of the Bank the terms of the loan was re-scheduled with remission of the interests. His brothers mortgaged a piece of land of their own as a matter of security to the loan and executed irrevocable power of attorney in favour of the bank. In view of the development he prayed, he might be allowed easy installments to pay of the outstanding dues on the loan account. Learned Judge passed an Order on 30-1-1994 disposing of execution case in terms of compromise allowing five years time to pay off the loan money with 3-monthly installments.

3. The 5 years time-frame expired on 30-1-1999 but the dues were not paid by the judgment-debtor on various excuses. The decree-holder Bank was ultimately led to file another application on 26-6-2002 for execution which gave rise to Execution Case No. 8 of 2002 in the Court of the Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Panchagarh, this time for realization of Tk. 9,74,985. The present petitioner along with his said two brothers appeared in the execution case and filed a joint written objection on 28-9-2002 denying the liability essentially on the ground of limitation. On 13-11-2002 an application was filed by the judgment-debtor asking for dismissal of the execution case basically on two grounds, namely, that the execution case was barred by limitation and that inclusion of his two brothers in the execution case is illegal as they were not party to the suit.

4. The application was heard by the learned Joint District Judge and upon hearing learned Judge rejected the same by his impugned order dated 13-11-2002 with observations, inter alia, that the judgment-debtor paid Tk. 2,06,000. He lastly paid Tk. 500 on 31-1-2001. The amount Tk. 9,74,925 is still outstanding which the judgment-debtor is liable to pay as per the conditions of the compromise.

5. The judgment-debtor and his said two brothers obtained this Rule challenging the aforesaid order of rejection on the common grounds agitated before the execution Court.

6. Mr. Mushfiqur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted at the outset that his case lies in the question of limitation and he was not inclined to focus much on the other point raised in the revisional application. Mr. Mushfiq submits by way of illustration that the decree was passed on 13-9-1988 and after 5 years from the date of decree an application was made for execution which gave rise to Execution Case No. 21 of 1993. On the compromise petition filed on 19-1-1994 the learned Judge passed his order on 30-1-1994 allowing the petitioner to pay off the outstanding dues within 5 years by 3-monthly installments. Five years' time allowed by the Court elapsed on 30-1-1999 allegedly without full payment of the dues. No steps for realization of money were taken by the Bank until 26-6-2002 on which date aforesaid execution case i.e., Execution Case No. 8 of 2002, was filed. This, Mr. Mushfiq submits, means that the second execution case was filed after 13 years 9 months from the date of decree; eight and half months from the date of disposal of the first execution in 1994 and at least 3½ years after the expiry of 5 years' time-frame allowed by Court. Therefore, he insisted, the execution case is plainly barred by limitation in view of Article 182 of the Limitation Act read with section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure, shortly, "the Code". In support of his contention Mr. Mushfiq referred to the case of Bangladesh Jatio Sainabaya Bank Limited vs Snngbad Daily Papers reported in 36 DLR 5 and another case ie, ADC Revenue, Palma vs Abdul Halim Mirth reported in 48 DLR (AD) 141.

7. Mr. Saidur Rahman learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party does not seem to oppose or controvert the sequence of facts presented by Mr. Mushfiqur Rahman. His contention is that the case is not barred by limitation in that where a decree or order directs any payment of money at a certain date the time limit is 12 years and computation of time starts from the date of default not from the date of decree or order. The second line of argument sought to be advanced by him is that his case is saved from the bar of limitation by virtue of sub-section (2) (a) of section 48 of the Code which says, inter alia, that if the decree-holder is prevented by the judgment-debtor from executing the decree by fraud or force the Court is competent to order execution even after 12 years provided by section 48(1)(b) of the Code.

8. In his bid to make out a case of 'fraud' Mr. Saidur Rahman urged upon us to take notice of the conduct of the judgment-debtor from the date of decree down to the date of filing the second execution case in 2002. He submits that the loan was taken against a small project under a special scheme of the Bank. It needs no mention that in all cases of loan against industrial project the Bank as financing institution naturally remains interested more in the success of the project than in ready realization of money. The judgment-debtor, he argued, taking advantage of the positive attitude of the Bank resorted to cunning devices from the outset to avoid payment. Soon after the decree was passed he began to overplay his sincerity to pay off the loan should the bank go soft on him. He set up plea that his mill was going sick and unless the interest was remitted and the loan terms were re-scheduled the project might fail and in the event none of the parties would benefit. The judgment-debtor, Mr. Rahman argued, in his bid to deceive the bank moved up to the Board of Directors well within 3 years' from decree and succeeded in persuading the authority about his bona fide by promising fresh-security against the loan through mortgage of land as mentioned above. The highest authority of the Bank stepped into the trap set by the judgment-debtor and after long negotiations remitted the interest of all kinds and re-scheduled the terms of the loan instead of taking recourse to execution process.

9. Mr. Rahman further contended that the judgment-debtor by reference to the re-scheduling of the loan as above filed the so-called compromise petition in Court and asked for easy installments for payment. Learned Court allowed five years' time with installments for payment which ended in January, 1999. The judgment-debtor continued with his secret design to deceive the bank and kept giving promises to pay the dues. Finally on 31-7-2001 he paid Tk. 500 as a gesture of his pretended good intention. The bank this time got disillusioned and realized the hidden design of the judgment-debtor to deceive the bank and finally brought the second execution case on 26-6-2002. All the incidents and conduct, Mr. Rahman contended, can only be explained upon the proposition of 'fraud' as contemplated in section 48(2) which, he contended, empowers the Court to order execution any time beyond 12 years provided by section 48(1) of the Code.

10. In support of his case Mr. Saidur Rahman referred to the case of Bishwanath Prasad Mahtha vs Lachhmi Narain reported in AIR 1935 Patna, 380 and another case i.e., Saifur Rahman vs Haider Shah reported in 19 DLR (SC) 433.

11. A plain reading of the revisional application vis-a-vis the law involved suggests that the fate of the Rule hinges more on technical question of law than on facts. The question that is mooted here is whether the execution case complained against is barred in view of section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Article 182 of the Limitation Act?

Section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure reads as follows:

"48.—(1) Where an application to execute a decree not being a decree granting an injunction has been made no order for the execution of the same decree shall be made upon any fresh application presented after the expiry of twelve years from:

a) the date of the decree sought to be executed, or,

b) where the decree or any subsequent order directs any payment of money or the delivery of any property to be to be made at a certain date or at recurring period, the date of default in making the payment or delivery in respect of which the application seeks to execute the decree.

(2) Nothing in this section shall be deemed—

a) to prevent the Court from ordering the execution of a decree upon an application presented after the expiry of the said term of twelve years, where the judgment-debtor has, by fraud or force, prevented the execution of the decree at some time within twelve years immediately before the date of application; or

b) to limit or otherwise affect the operation of article 183 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908 (X of 1908).

12. In the case of Bangladesh Jatya Samabaya Bank reported in 36 DLR (AD) 5 and ADC Revenue case reported in 48 DLR (AD) 141, cited by Mr. Mushfiqur Rahman the view taken by the Appellate Division is that 12 years limitation for execution of decree is the maximum limit allowed by law but the first execution must, however, be made within 3 years from decree and no subsequent application, if any, should exceed 3 years from the final order passed in the preceding execution case. In ADC Revenue Case (supra) our Appellate Division held:

".. both section 48 CPC and Article 182 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act provide the period of limitation for execution of a decree. The Civil Procedure Code fixes the longest period whereas the Limitation Act fixes the earliest period to take the first step in execution and the Sub-sequent steps known as steps-in-aid. an application for execution has, therefore, to satisfy first Article 182 of the Limitation Act being the earliest period prescribed and then also section 48 CPC which prescribed the maximum period of limitation. if the execution petitions is hit by any of the two it is to fail."

<u>13. The above decision of the Appellate Division came in the factual background of condoning the delay in making petitions for execution beyond 3 years time provided by Article 182 of the Limitation Act finally exceeding the outer limit of 12 years provided by section 48 of the Code by the trial Court on ground of continued insanity of the decree-holder and affirmed by the High Court Division in revision holding that section 48 of the Code did not have application in the case.</u>

14. it is clear from the above decisions that section 48(1) of the Code and Article 182 of the Limitation Act are construed by the Appellate Division to mean that there is both earliest and longest time for putting decree into execution and violation of either of the limitations is held to be fatal.

15. In the instant case it appears that second execution case was filed apparently beyond 3 years' from the date of decree. The judgment-debtor does not deny the fact either. The second execution case was filed in 2002 which by simple calculation is beyond 12 years from the decree. In needs hardly be mentioned that in view of the decision of the Appellate Division the execution case is barred by limitation. But that is not the only point raised here. The second and the most crucial point raised is distinctly removed from the issue decided by the Appellate Division. Mr. Saidur Rahman, learned Advocate, besides his first line of defense, has tried to make out a case of fraud as contemplated under sub-section (2) of section 48 of the Code.

16. The case sought to be canvassed by Mr. Saidur Rahman is that the judgment-debtor by his fraudulent conduct prevented the decree-holder from taking out execution against him within time. Now the Court is competent to see whether the decree-holder is so prevented and, if it is so found, can order execution even after expiry of 12 years' time as per sub-section (2) of section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

<u>17. Sub-section (2) of section 48 of the Code, as is quoted above, is all overriding clause that empowers executing Court to order execution even beyond 12 years' time if it is found that the judgment-debtor, by fraud or force, has prevented the decree-holder from executing the decree at some time within the period of 12 year immediately before the date of application. The scope and ambit of 'fraud' for the purpose of the section is now settled more or less.</u>

18. For the purpose of section 48(2) of the Code the word 'fraud' is liberally construed by the superior Courts. In Saifur Rahamn vs Haidar Shah, 19 DLR (SC) 433, the then Pakistan Supreme Court held:

"The term 'fraud' in this section has to be interpreted in liberal sense as including any improper means resorted to for preventing execution. It covers not only deceit but also circumvention."

19. In Biswanath vs Lachhmi, AIR 1935 Patna 380, a Division Bench of Patna High Court held: "What is quite clearly contemplated, apart from the definition of the term itself, (fraud) is some action on the part of the judgment-debtor which prevents the decree-holder from taking out execution proceedings and thus allowing time to run against him or some action by judgment-debtor which entices the decree-holder to hold his hand"

20. Similar view has been taken in Gobardlzan vs Daudayal, AIR 1931 All 301; Raj Sham vs Daman; 11 CWN 440 and Adaikappa vs Netsan, AIR 1931 Mad 381 and Abdul Khadir, P. vs Ajiyar Ahmmad reported in 35 ILR Mad 670.

<u>21. Power of the Court appears to be spell out in no uncertain terms that if the decree-holder is found to be prevented by the judgment-debtor by fraud or force from taking out execution it is competent in its discretion to override the 12 years, time prescribed by law and direct execution of decree anytime beyond the limitation.</u>

22. Reverting back to the facts it transpires that there are some admitted positions, namely, that a certain amount of loan was taken by the petitioner No.1 (judgment-debtor) from the opposite party bank that he failed to pay off the loan in full till today far less on schedule. The bank filed two execution cases both beyond time prescribed by law. The judgment-debtor has seized of the weakness of the execution case and urges upon for the right vested in him due on the failure of the decree-holder to execute his decree.

23. A close scrutiny of factual developments around failure of the decree-holder bank in taking out execution in time presents a peculiar scenario of the conduct of the judgment-debtor. A decree-holder, that too a bank has no earthly reason to avoid execution. Curiously for the bank, it filed both the execution cases beyond time. This is self-explanatory and must have some or other back-story that consistently prevented the bank from initiation of execution cases.

24. Record shows that the decree was passed in 1988 and first execution case was filed in 1992. The so-called compromise petition suggests that the judgment-debtor moved to the Board of Directors of the decree-holder bank for remission of the interests, rescheduling of the loan and other facilities. It appears that the highest authority of the bank was finally prevailed over and remission of interests and re-scheduling etc was made. In taking the advantage the judgment-debtor got his two brothers tagged along and made them to provide fresh security against the loan by mortgaging pieces of land of their own and to execute irrevocable power of attorney in favour of the bank. The entire process from initiation to the end entails consumption of time. Mr. Saidur Rahmart, learned Advocate submitted with emphasis that the tidbit started immediately after the decree was passed i.e., far before the expiry of 3 years' limitation for execution. In view of the volume of works and runaround involved in the job we have no reason to disbelieve the case of the decree-holder that the tadbir so started. If it is so the decree-holder would naturally prefer pursuing the matter outside Court and thereby incur delay in filing the execution case. The delay so incurred, in our opinion, may reasonably be explained upon the proposition that the decree-holder was prevented by fraud in taking out execution at sometime within 3 years from decree. In Abdul Khadir (supra), a Division Bench of the Madras High Court made the following observations:

"Fraud at sometime within 12 years period to the application for execution being sufficient to entitle the decree-holder to ask for execution, it is clear that it is not incumbent on him to show continuous diligence during all the time prior to the application. The language of the section also shows clearly that the decree-holder is not bound to show that, but for the fraud or force complained of, he would have realized the fruit of his decree. All that has to be proved is that the judgment-debtor, by fraud or force, at sometime prevented the execution that is in my Opinion, made the decree-holder's attempts to execute at the time to which fraud relates, unsuccessful."

25. Payment of some money in 2001 by the judgment-debtor indicates that he kept the decree-holder in good humour althrough and by fraudulent means prevented the bank from going for execution of the decree.

26. The judgment-debtor being guilty of fraud within the meaning of section 48(2) it must, therefore, be held that he prevented the decree-holder by fraud from taking out execution against him and thereby keeps the decree alive so as to be put into execution. The execution case filed after 12 years period from decree thus being protected under section 48(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure is maintainable.

In the result, the Rule is discharged. The impugned order passed by the executing Court is maintained and the order of stay granted earlier by this Court is hereby vacated.

There shall, however, be no order as to cost.

Communicate a copy of this judgment at once.

End.

full_judgment:
This rule is directed against the Judgment and decree dated 5-6-2004 Passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla, in Title Appeal No. 210 of 2001 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 5-7-2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chauddagram, Comilla, in Title Suit No. 44 of 1994 decreeing the suit.

2. Facts, in short, are that a suit for partition being No. 44 of 1994 was decreed ascertaining the plaintiffs share to the extent of 1.05½ acres. The defendant Nos. 1-7 and 53 also got a saham to the extent of 36 decimals. That preliminary decree was not challenged in appeal.

3. The plaintiff submitted an application for making the decree final and accordingly a Commissioner was appointed. The learned Advocate Commissioner serving due notice upon the parties executed a commission and submitted a report making final allotment of saham. The report was objected by the defendants, contending inter alit?, that one of the huts of the defendant was allotted to the saham of the plaintiffs share and the pathway used by the defendants was allotted to the saham of the plaintiff making a great inconvenience to them. The learned Advocate Commissioner was examined in Court and was cross-examined. The learned Assistant Judge after considering the evidence on record accepted the Commissioner's report, rejected the objection and made the decree final by the Judgment and decree dated 8-7-2001 against which the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 210 of 2001. The Court of appeal dismissed the appeal and affirmed the final decree by the impugned judgment and decree against which the instant Rule.

4. Mr Subhas Chandra Saha, the learned Advocate for the petitioner appearing for the petitioner took me through the commissioner report, objection submitted against the Commission report and the evidence on record. He submitted that as per own admission of the Advocate Commissioner a part of the defendant's homestead was allotted to the saham of the plaintiff and as such the final decree is liable to be set aside and a fresh commission required to be made for effecting equitable partition. He further submitted that the pathway of the defendant for going to the pond has been allotted to the saham of the plaintiff by which the defendants are facing very much inconvenience.

5. Mr AU Ahmed with Mr Md Mesbahul Islam, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party on the other hand submitted that the learned Advocate Commissioner after serving due notice to the parties executed commissioner in presence of both the parties and submitted report maintaining present possession of the parties as far as practicable.

6. Mr AU Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the opposite party submitted that for effecting equitable partition is not possible to maintain the entire possession of any party who are in possession in more land than that of his share. Since the defendants were in possession in the land more than that of their share, the Commissioner had to allot some land from the possession of the defendant and that was within the direction of the Court as per writ issued to the Commissioner.

7. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates. I have perused the commission report, objection filed by the defendant against the report, the evidence on record and the impugned judgment and decree.

<u>8. In a suit for partition usually some of the co-sharers hold excessive land than that of their actual share and the co-sharer who holds minimum land in possession comes before the Court with a suit for partition.</u>

<u>9. It is not unusual that at the time of Final Partition some of the possessor would be affected and some of the decree holder would be benefited.</u>

<u>10. It is also not possible that the entire possession of any party could be maintained at the time of effecting partition.</u>

11. In view of the above although the submissions as made by Mr Saha appears to be meaningful but since the defendants were allotted saham maintaining 36 decimals of land, it would not be justified to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. Since the defendant's have not been allotted share Sesser than that of their actual saham, I do not find any cogent ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree.

12. In view of the above I find no merit in the Rule. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 5-6-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla, in Title Appeal No. 210 of 2001 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 5-7-2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Chauddagram, Comilla, in Title Suit No. 44 of 1994 decreeing the suit is hereby affirmed. The order of stay dated 11-12-2004 granted by this Court stands vacated.

Records of the lower Court be send down.

End.
